site.name: Clark Tunnel
site.location: Vasco No. 6 workings / Boulder County Tungsten Mining District
overview: Clark Tunnel was a documented tunnel level within the Vasco No. 6 tungsten-mine workings in Boulder County's historic tungsten district near the former village of Tungsten.
Federal and Colorado mining records show that the tunnel intersected a series of named tungsten veins and provided underground access through a large part of the connected mine system.

timeline.text: Contemporary mining-industry reporting said Clark Tunnel had reached about 800 feet and had cut four promising tungsten-bearing veins while Boulder Tungsten Production Company operated the property.

U.S. Geological Survey mapping identified Clark Tunnel as Level 3 of the Vasco No. 6 mine, while Colorado's tungsten-mine inventory documented the tunnel extending about 2,150 feet and intersecting multiple named veins.

moreHistory: U.S. Geological Survey Professional Paper 245 labels the third level of the Vasco No. 6 mine as the Clark Tunnel level and includes it on the mine's longitudinal projection.

Colorado's Tungsten Mines of Colorado places Barker No. 1 about 200 feet inside Clark Tunnel, Barker No. 2 about 450 feet inside, Barker No. 3 about 650 feet inside, and Barker No. 4 about 720 feet inside. The same inventory describes Clark Tunnel itself as about 2,150 feet long and intersecting the Barker, Vasco 6, Murphy, Five, and Hurricane Hill reef systems.

A mapped historic tunnel locality at approximately 39.9700, -105.4800 is retained for Clark Tunnel. The point identifies the documented tunnel locality and does not imply that a surviving portal has been field verified or is safe or publicly accessible.
